text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV 2 — high p99 latency observed for /streaming/v1 (region: us-west-2). Auto-page to on-call. Metrics: p95=420ms (SLO 300ms), p99=5.8s (SLO 800ms). Error spike: 504s from proxy. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail-latency

maria (oncall): acked, jumping on. tagging kevin and oliver for infra + proxies. Starting quick blast checklist.

maria (oncall): first-pass impact: ~3% of requests showing chunking stalls (clients see long pauses between chunks). Affected endpoints: /streaming/v1, /realtime/chat-stream. Origins point to envoy proxies returning 504s with upstream write timeouts.

kevin: looking at deploys — no model/runtime change in last 45m. One config push to envoy-frontend 2h ago (conn pool tuning). Rolling back that config is an option.

oliver: grabbing logs from proxy cluster:
```
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z envoy [warning] upstream timeout while writing response to client, downstream connection stalled
2026-03-15T10:14:02Z proxy-monitor connection_pool exhausted for host streaming-svc-02
```

sam: metrics: backend latency (app pods) p50=90ms p95=350ms p99=1.2s. Proxy write latency ballooning to p99=6.5s. Heap/CPU on app nodes normal. Network drops low. Suggests proxy-level buffering/connection saturation.

maria (oncall): can we confirm number of active streaming sockets per proxy? if clients slow-reading, that can exhaust connection slots.

kevin: querying counts: `kubectl exec -it envoy-frontend-0 -- curl -s localhost:9901/stats | grep streams_active` -> returns ~4.2k active streams on each frontend pod (normal is ~800).

elaine: customer-eng: we already have one enterprise customer on escalation (CorpA). They report intermittent freezes in their live agent UI. Please include customer impact in status update.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan (short): 1) reduce accept/concurrency on frontends to limit head-of-line, 2) enable immediate proxy idle timeouts to free stuck connections, 3) route new traffic to fallback pool with smaller chunk sizes. Rolling changes carefully.

kevin: implementing quick throttle: patch envoy config to lower `per_connection_buffer_limit_bytes` and set `upstream_idle_timeout` to 10s. Pushing to one pod for canary.

kevin: canary push logs: `kubectl apply -f envoy-patch-canary.yaml` -> applied to envoy-frontend-0. Watching metrics.

maria (oncall): running synthetic streaming test against canary: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" https://staging/streaming/v1?test=chunk`

sam: synthetic shows chunk interval stable at 200ms for canary vs 2s for old config. Good. p99 proxy write latency on canary now 600ms.

oliver: scaling frontends up by 2 pods to help connection headroom: `kubectl scale deploy envoy-frontend --replicas=6`. Doing now.

incident-bot: NOTE: paging rule: SEV >=2 notify infra, oncall, and customer-eng.

maria (oncall): customer update draft: \"We're actively mitigating elevated tail latency on streaming endpoints; we've deployed a partial proxy config change and scaled frontends. Some customers may see intermittent stalls; we're prioritizing affected customers. ETA for broader mitigation: 30-45m.\" Any objections?

customer-eng: send it, include that CorpA is being handled with priority support call.

kevin: after canary success, rolling patch to remaining frontends with 2m stagger: `for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=envoy-frontend -o name); do kubectl rollout restart $p; sleep 120; done`

oliver: note — we also added a temporary connection-limiter: `envoy.filters.network.connection_limiter` configured to 1000 concurrent streams per worker. This prevents a single proxy from hoarding all streams.

sam: monitoring: p99 for proxy write latency falling from 6.5s -> 900ms within 8 minutes of canary roll. p95 now 280ms. Throughput stable.

maria (oncall): good. now need to triage root cause: why did connection counts spike? any traffic pattern change?

kevin: pulled access logs: spike in clients using `curl -N` from a small set of IP ranges (likely a customer-side bot) with very slow read rates, holding SSE connections open but slow consuming. Those clients overwhelmed frontends.

elaine: reached out to CorpA — they confirm a misconfigured client-side integration hitting long-poll with tiny read buffer. They're coordinating a fix.

maria (oncall): root cause hypothesis: a mix of slow-consuming clients + aggressive connection pool config on envoy (recent change) created per-proxy slot exhaustion and upstream write stalls. Mitigations: config rollback vs permanent tuning + per-tenant rate-limits for streaming.

kevin: action items (short term): 1) keep patched envoy config rolled out, 2) keep frontend replicas at 6 for 1h, 3) add streaming connection limiter per IP range, 4) add alert for streams_active > 1200 per pod.

oliver: infra follow-ups (postmortem): investigate why config change was rolled without canary for high-traffic endpoints, add smoke-tests for streaming behavior, and add automated throttles for slow-consumers.

maria (oncall): handing over to kevin for overnight monitoring and postmortem lead. Summary for handoff:
- incident started 2026-03-15T10:13Z (auto-page).
- impact: streaming tail latency p99 up to 6.5s, ~3% of streaming requests stalled; one enterprise customer (CorpA) reported UI freezes.
- immediate mitigations applied: envoy buffer/idle timeout tuning, connection limiter, scaled frontends, route fallback for heavy customers.
- current status: p99 stabilized ~850-950ms; p95 within SLO. No data loss; no model rollback.

kevin: taking over monitoring. I'll run 15m checks and update status. If p99 > 1.5s re-escalate to SRE channel.

maria (oncall): thanks team. leaving note in incident tracker: https://redwood/incidents/3350000000 - assign kevin as owner.

kevin: assigning postmortem. initial RCA: client slow-consumers + proxy pool tuning. Longer-term fixes: per-tenant connection quotas, improved canary for proxy configs, and streaming smoke-tests.

sam: I'll prepare graphs (p50/p95/p99 for app/proxy, active stream counts) for the postmortem.

elaine: I'll coordinate the customer communication and let CorpA know we implemented throttles and they're safe to reconnect.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigations in place). Final state: reduced p99 to <1s, monitoring enabled. Close after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
